channel.title: Feminism In India - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Feminism In India (feminisminindia.com)

item.title: Invisible By Design: How India’s Construction Sector Systematically Marginalises Women Workers
item.description: Women construction workers' labour is constant, visible and physically demanding but it's not acknowledged in policy conversations.

item.title: Sara Arjun, Ranveer Singh And The "Age"-Old Question That Bollywood Keeps Dodging
item.description: Age gaps in Bollywood are not transgressive, they are routine, which makes them all the more scarier, as is seen in the 'Dhurandhar' pairing.

item.title: Power, Consumption And Gender: An Analysis Of Barbara Kruger's Political Art
item.description: Barbara Kruger rose to prominence through her artwork ‘Untitled (Your body is a battleground)’ for pro-choice Washington rally in 1989.

item.title: Who Gets To Dance? Gender, Power, And Exclusion In Indian Classical Dance Forms
item.description: Learn how gender dynamics play a crucial role in the practice and perception of Indian classical dance forms.

item.title: Man-Repellent Makeup And The Politics Of Beauty
item.description: Man-repellent makeup presents a strategy to question who gets to be visible and safe, and who ultimately profits from defiance.

item.title: Walls Of Dissent: Art, Graffiti, And Visual Resistance In Kashmir
item.description: Graffiti teaches us the idea that resistance is not necessarily loud or institutionalized, but sometimes it sits quietly on the walls.

item.title: Why Audre Lorde's Work Remains As Relevant As Ever
item.description: Learn about Audre Lorde's contributions as a poet and academic, and how her work continues to inspire inclusion and community.

item.title: Fasting, Faith, And Female Bodies: A Feminist Reading Of Vrat Kathas
item.description: The vrat kathas functions as a form of ritual art, performed, repeated, and aesthetically framed, through which social norms are not merely transmitted but also transformed into sacred meaning.

item.title: Meira Kumar: How A Dalit Woman Reshaped Indian Politics From The Speaker's Chair
item.description: Meira Kumar is a politician and Speaker of the 15th Lok Sabha, who has left her mark on the field of Indian politics.

item.title: The Rural Road To Patriarchy: Land, Labour, And The Gendered Cost Of Reform
item.description: The reforms aimed at the economic, political and social mobility of the rural masses have been largely discriminatory to women.
